mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal blood flow and inhibit prostaglandin-mediated vasodilation, while thiazide diuretics cause volume depletion and electrolyte loss, together increasing risk of acute kidney injury, hyperkalemia, and reduced antihypertensive efficacy.
action: Monitor serum creatinine, potassium, and blood pressure closely; consider alternative analgesia or limit ketorolac duration to ≤5 days; ensure adequate hydration and assess renal function baseline and during therapy.
